content.comment_body: I am looking to connect an analog output signal from a UV Meter into the analog input on a [product_name] controller. The meter outputs a voltage signal ranging from 0 to 1V, where 0V corresponds to 0 mJ and 1V to a maximum of 1000mJ. The meter has a two-wire output (orange and white), and I'm considering connecting orange to the controller’s supply voltage and white directly to the input. Is a resistor required in between? According to the meter specs, the output impedance is 1k ohm, and it recommends an input impedance greater than 1M ohm for accurate measurement. If the input impedance is too low, readings may be inaccurate. In this setup, the controller acts as the recorder. Does this controller’s input impedance meet the recommended specification for accurate measurement? Any advice is appreciated! Thanks!
It seems you should wire the output positive terminal to the analog input (I7 or I8) and the output negative terminal to the negative power connection of the controller.
